questions.q:
What is the amplitude of the graph of function $f(x) = \frac{1}{2}\cos(3x + \pi)$, shown in the standard $(x,y)$ coordinate plane?

<svg viewBox="0 0 200 120" width="200" height="120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <path d="M10,60 Q30,10 50,60 T90,60 T130,60 T170,60" fill="none" stroke="black"/>
  <line x1="0" y1="60" x2="180" y2="60" stroke="black"/>
  <line x1="90" y1="0" x2="90" y2="120" stroke="black"/>
</svg>
questions.explain: For a trigonometric function of the form $f(x) = A\cos(Bx + C) + D$, the amplitude is given by $|A|$. Here, the coefficient $A$ is $\frac{1}{2}$, so the amplitude is $\frac{1}{2}$.
